  1. Prime Minister Narendra Modi calls upon Indian industries to seize new opportunities arising from country’s growth story.
  2. Home Minister Amit Shah asserts, government is developing integrated system to enable police stations nationwide to work under unified anti-terror Strategy.
  3. India and Japan hold Foreign and Defence Ministers’ Dialogue in Tokyo; Agree to fast-track defence deals, and strengthen maritime security cooperation.

Prime Minister Narendra Modi has said, India’s growth story is creating new opportunities and called upon Indian industries to be prepared to seize them. Mr Modi was addressing the gathering on centenary convention of industry body Federation of Indian Chambers of Commerce and Industry (FICCI) at Bharat Mandapam in New Delhi today. The Prime Minister said FICCI has witnessed significant achievements in India’s industrial sector over the past 100 years. 

 

 

The Prime Minister said India is now the world’s fastest-growing major economy, with a projected growth rate of around seven per cent. He said the latest World Bank report, which states that 50 crore Indians have overcome poverty in just 12 to 13 years, is a matter of great pride for the nation.

 

 

Speaking at the event, Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal said that Viksit Bharat 2047 is not merely another agenda or target, but a collective national resolve driven by the energy and contribution of every Indian.

Home Minister Amit Shah has said, the country is now moving towards establishing a coordinated system to combat terrorism. He said, the government is building a system in which all police stations across the country will work on a unified strategy to combat terrorism. Mr Shah stated this while addressing the inaugural session of a two-day counter-terrorism conference organised by National Intelligence Agency in New Delhi. The Home Minister said, the government’s zero tolerance policy against terrorism under the leadership of Prime Minister Narendra Modi is yielding positive results. Mentioning the recent elimination of Lashkar terrorist Latif Bhat, Mr Shah said, the entire Kashmir has become free from terrorism. He said, this situation has come about after 35 years.

External Affairs Minister Dr S. Jaishankar and Defence Minister Rajnath Singh co-chaired the fourth Foreign and Defence Ministers’ (2+2) Dialogue with their Japanese counterparts Toshimitsu Motegi and Shinjiro Koizumi in Tokyo today. During the meeting, the two countries agreed to fast-track defence agreements related to the Unified Complex Radio Antenna (UNICORN) stealth naval mast project. The move aims to strengthen maritime security cooperation and expand joint defence manufacturing between the two countries.

 

 

 

Addressing a joint press briefing, Mr Singh said the discussions covered a wide range of issues under the two countries’ Special Strategic and Global Partnership.

 

 

Dr Jaishankar said cooperation between India and Japan aims to promote a multipolar Asia and a multipolar world.

 

 

Later, in a joint statement, both countries unequivocally and strongly condemned terrorism and violent extremism in all its form and manifestations, including cross-border terrorism, and called for action against all United Nations-listed terrorist groups and entities.

Severe Cyclonic Storm Akvan over Bay of Bengal is moving north-northwestwards. It is likely to cross the Andhra Pradesh and Odisha coasts between Narsapur and Puri, passing close to the east of Gopalpur, by tomorrow noon. The India Meteorological Department said the cyclone has been moving at a speed of 13 kilometres per hour over the past six hours. Wind speeds at the time of landfall are expected to reach 90 to 100 kilometres per hour, with gusts of up to 110 kilometres per hour. Odisha and Andhra Pradesh governments have stepped up their preparedness to deal with the impending cyclone. In Odisha, more than one lakh five thousand people have already been evacuated to safer locations. Our correspondent has the details

 

 

 

“As a precautionary measure, the state government has already started the evacuation process in view of the impending cyclone. The government has set up over nine thousand shelters and deployed over 3 hundred emergency response teams, including NDRF and ODRAF, across vulnerable places in several districts. As of now, over 1 lakh 5 thousand people have been evacuated and shifted to safer places. Chief Minister Mohan Charan Majhi said the government is making all necessary preparations, with priority being given to ensure “zero casualties”. The Puri Shree Jagannath Temple Administration urged devotees to plan their visits in line with weather advisories in view of the Cyclonic storm. In view of Cyclone Akvan, Indian Railways has cancelled and rescheduled train services. With SN Patnaik this is Smrutirekha for Akashvani News Cuttack.”

 

 

 

The Andhra Pradesh Government has also intensified its preparations to tackle the approaching cyclone. More from our correspondent:

 

 

 

“Heavy rainfall is likely in parts of Srikakulam district. Moderate rain may occur in Vizianagaram, Parvathipuram Manyam, Alluri Sitarama Raju, Polavaram, Visakhapatnam, Anakapalli and Kakinada districts. Strong winds may uproot trees and damage temporary structures. Low-lying areas may also face waterlogging. The Andhra Pradesh State Disaster Management Authority has advised fishermen not to venture into the sea. People living along the North Andhra coast have been asked to remain alert. Farmers have been advised to protect harvested paddy from rain and follow official advisories. Allu Murali Akashvani News,Vijaywada.”

 

 

 

Under the influence of Severe Cyclonic Storm Akvan, several districts of West Bengal are also experiencing rainfall.

The Government has revised the validity period of Pollution Under Control (PUC) certificates for different categories of vehicles. The Ministry of Road Transport and Highways has amended the Central Motor Vehicles Rules, 1989, in this regard. According to a Gazette notification, the validity of PUC certificates will now depend on the vehicle’s emission standards, category and age.

 

 

“Under the amended rules, vehicles complying with BS-I, BS-II and BS-III emission norms will have a PUC certificate valid for three months, while vehicles complying with BS-IV norms will have a validity of six months. For non-transport vehicles complying with BS-VI emission norms, the certificate will be valid for three years for vehicles up to six years old. While for vehicles more than six years and up to ten years old, the validity will be for one year. For vehicles older than ten years, the validity will be six months. In the case of transport vehicles complying with BS-VI norms, the certificate validity for vehicles up to six years old will be for two years. The validity of the certificate will be one year for vehicles of more than six years and up to ten years old, and six months for vehicles older than ten years. Akshit Vaidyan for Akashvani News, Delhi”

The 57th International Film Festival of India (IFFI) 2026 is all set to begin in Goa tomorrow. We have a report:

 

 

“Goa is all set to host the 57th International Film Festival of India (IFFI) 2026, with preparations in place to welcome filmmakers, artists and cinema enthusiasts from across the world. The opening day will feature the screening of the film, ‘Fatherland’, directed by Polish filmmaker Paweł Pawlikowski. The film will be be screened at INOX Panjim from 2 PM, ahead of the grand opening ceremony at 5 PM at the Dr Shyama Prasad Mukherjee Indoor Stadium in Goa. Among the major additions this year are the two new sections, Films About Films and the Animation segment. Introduced for the first time in IFFI’s history, ‘Films About Films’ will feature five international productions exploring the lives, creative journeys and legacies of filmmakers, actors and cinema itself. While the Animation segment will present five acclaimed films from Japan, France, China, Singapore and the United States, highlighting the artistic possibilities and emotional depth of animated storytelling. The festival will also feature special showcases of Indian and international cinema, including a focus on BRICS films. Furthermore, Spain has been named the Country of Honour, while Russia will participate as the Partner Country. With Nikhil Upadhyay this is Vishnu from Goa”.

Union Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman today chaired the sixth Pre-Budget Consultation with experts and stakeholders from the Information Technology sector in New Delhi. The meeting was held as part of the preparations for the forthcoming Union Budget 2027-28.

 

 


Later in the day, the Finance Minister chaired the seventh Pre-Budget Consultation with experts from the infrastructure, energy and sustainability sectors.

Chief of Defence Staff General Anil Chauhan has said, Humanitarian Assistance and Disaster Relief reflects India’s commitment to human security, both within the country and across its wider neighbourhood. He was addressing the media at Jamnagar Air Force Station on the third and concluding day of the Annual Joint Humanitarian Assistance and Disaster Relief Exercise, Exercise Sahayata Setu, which began on Tuesday.

The leaders of the United States, China and Russia today held their first-ever trilateral summit in Shenzhen to discuss key international security issues. US President Donald Trump, Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin met on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation Summit. 

 

 

The US President in his opening remarks, called for cooperation among the three major powers to reduce nuclear weapons and prevent their proliferation.

 

 

Later, unprecedented trilateral summit concluded with the adoption of a four-point ‘Declaration Towards Peace’. It called for reforms in the United Nations and outlined plans to increase the production and supply of refined petroleum products to address the global energy crisis.

In Badminton, Lakshya Sen, Kidambi Srikanth and Rakshitha Ramraj have advanced to the quarter finals of Singles event at Hong Kong Open Super 500 tournament.

 

 

In Men’s Singles, Lakshya defeated Rasmus Gemke of Denmark, in the prequarter finals while Kidambi upset Yoo Tae-bin. In Women’s Singles, Ramaraj overpowered Chen Yufei of China, in the pre-quarterfinals.

 

 

Men’s doubles pair of Satwiksairaj Rankireddy and Chirag Shetty stormed into the last eight. The Indian duo defeated Malaysia’s Nur Mohd Azriyn Ayub and Tan Wee Kiong with a straight-game win.

At the Women’s Asian Hockey Champions Trophy, Defending champions India began their title defence with a convincing 4-1 victory over Malaysia in Bhopal today.

 

 

India, three-time champions, will be looking to continue their winning momentum as they aim to retain the title and secure their fourth Asian Champions Trophy crown.

Prime Minister Narendra Modi today chaired a meeting of Council of Ministers at Bharat Mandapam in New Delhi. In a social media post, Mr Modi said, there was extensive discussions on good governance initiatives. As the news agency PTI reported, elevation of 50 crore people from below the poverty line and elimination of Naxals were the two key subjects that were discussed in the meeting. The meeting hailed the Modi government’s poverty elevation programmes. A number of issues like governance, reforms and outreach to women and youth on welfare and development schemes were also discussed at the meeting.

President Droupadi Murmu today said that India has achieved unprecedented expansion of infrastructure, revolutionary digital transformation, financial inclusion, social development in the last ten years. The President made these remarks while addressing the valedictory ceremony of the centenary celebrations of Shri Ram College of Commerce in New Delhi.

External Affairs Minister Dr S Jaishankar has called for strengthening India-Japan cooperation in key areas, including economic security, advanced manufacturing, semiconductors, critical minerals, clean energy and defence. Addressing the inaugural event of Raisina Tokyo 2026, Dr Jaishankar said, the rapidly changing global landscape has made trusted partnerships, supply chain diversification and stronger national capacities increasingly important.

 

 

 

Dr Jaishankar said India and Japan, as leading nations of the Indo-Pacific committed to a free and open region, must deepen reliable cooperation while safeguarding their national interests and promoting regional stability. He said, India and Japan are members of the Quad, partners in the G4 initiative for United Nations reform and participants in the East Asia Summit.

 

 

 

India and Japan are set to review their bilateral defence ties and strategic cooperation as Defence Minister Rajnath Singh and External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar reached Tokyo today to attend the fourth edition of the 2+2 ministerial dialogue tomorrow. The two leaders will co-chair the Foreign and Defence Ministers’ Dialogue (2+2) with their Japanese counterparts, Shinjiro Koizumi and Toshimitsu Motegi. In a social media post, Mr Singh said, he would review progress in defence and security cooperation and explore new opportunities to deepen collaboration in technology, maritime security and regional stability.

 

 

<><><> 

 

 

Defence Minister Rajnath Singh today said, country’s defence sector is moving beyond self-reliance to strengthen its global standing, with defence production and exports expanding at an unprecedented pace. Addressing members of the Indian community in Tokyo, Mr. Singh said the growing capabilities of the Armed Forces, coupled with indigenous defence manufacturing, were taking country’s defence strength to new heights.

Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal today held a bilateral meeting with Italy’s Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation Antonio Tajani in Rome. Speaking on the occasion, Mr Goyal reaffirmed country’s commitment to taking the economic partnership with Italy to new heights and achieving the ambitious bilateral trade target of 20 billion euros by 2029.

 

 

During the meeting, Antonio Tajani also said the free trade agreement signed between the European Union and India is a further boost to increasing Italy’s presence in India and India’s presence in Italy.

Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman today chaired the fifth Pre-Budget Consultation with the stakeholders from the capital markets, banking, financial services and insurance sector in connection with the forthcoming Union Budget 2027-28, in New Delhi. The meeting was attended by Secretaries, Department of Economic Affairs, and Department of Financial Services and by Chief Economic Adviser to the Government V Anantha Nageswaran.

The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has said that the severe cyclonic storm Akvan over the south Bay of Bengal has moved north-northwestwards and lay centred 560 kilometres east of Chennai today. It is likely to cross North Andhra Pradesh, Yanam and South Odisha coasts on Friday as a severe cyclonic storm. The Met Department has advised the fishermen not to venture into Westcentral and Northwest Bay of Bengal till 21st November. The weather agency has issued a red colour warning for very heavy to extremely heavy rainfall over Coastal Andhra Pradesh and Odisha during the next two days. Meanwhile, the Andhra Pradesh government has geared up preparedness. A report:

 

 

 

“The Andhra Pradesh government has put the state machinery on high alert and directed all departments to remain fully prepared for the next 48 hours. District and mandal control rooms will function round the clock to monitor the situation and respond to requests for assistance. Thirteen NDRF teams and eleven SDRF teams, besides fire service personnel, have been kept ready for emergency operations. Arrangements have been made to evacuate people from unsafe areas to relief centres. Power distribution companies have stocked essential materials and kept emergency teams ready for speedy restoration of damaged infrastructure. People in coastal areas have been advised to stay indoors and avoid unnecessary travel. The government has urged people to follow official weather warnings and not believe unverified information on social media. Allu Murali, Akashvani News, Vijayawada.”

 

 

 

Odisha Government has stepped up evacuation, deployed emergency response teams and placed vulnerable districts on high alert. More from our Correspondent –

 

 

 

“Odisha Government has identified more than two lakh people for possible evacuation and is preparing to shift vulnerable residents to safer locations. The Special Relief Commissioner has directed Collectors of six districts—Ganjam, Gajapati, Rayagada, Kandhamal, Malkangiri and Koraput—to identify landslide-prone villages and road stretches and take precautionary measures. The IMD has issued red warnings for Ganjam, Gajapati, Kandhamal, Puri, Jagatsinghpur and Kendrapara for tomorrow, forecasting extremely heavy rainfall at isolated places. Schools, colleges and Anganwadi centres in six districts—Ganjam, Gajapati, Puri, Jagatsinghpur, Kendrapara and Kandhamal—will remain closed until Saturday. The State Government has also cancelled leave for all government employees until Sunday. Prakash Dash for Akashvani News, Bhubaneswar.”

 

 

 

 

Railways Minister, Ashwini Vaishnaw reviewed Indian Railways’ preparedness in view of the approaching Cyclone Akvan. The Minister directed railway officials to take all necessary precautionary measures, with special emphasis on passenger safety, protection of railway infrastructure, regulation of train operations and advance restoration planning.

Iran widened its attacks on its Gulf neighbours today, firing on a US air base in Kuwait and several times at Bahrain in what appeared to be retaliation for American strikes the day before. The early morning attacks came after a US fighter jet struck a Revolutionary Guard missile launch site yesterday on Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz.

The stage is all set for the 57th International Film Festival of India (IFFI) 2026, which is set to begin in Goa from the 20th of this month. The nine-day festival will bring together filmmakers, artists and cinema enthusiasts from across the world, celebrating the diversity of global cinema. Among the highlights this year is a dedicated new Animation segment, celebrating the artistry and emotional depth of animated storytelling. More from our Correspondent:

 

 

 

“Animation has the unique ability to bring drawings to life and tell stories that connect with audiences across cultures and generations. Adding a new dimension to this year’s festival, the 57th International Film Festival of India has introduced a dedicated Animation segment featuring five international animated feature films from Japan, France, China, Singapore and the United States. The selection includes Cherry and Virgin from Japan, Jim Queen from France, Light Pillar from China, Magic Atlas from Singapore and Ray Gunn from the United States. The films explore a range of themes, including love, identity, loneliness, memory and resistance. Through this new segment, IFFI aims to showcase the creative possibilities of animation and bring diverse international stories to festival audiences. With Vishnu and Alex, this is Saira Mujtaba, from Panaji, Goa.”

Ace Indian shuttlers, Lakshya Sen and Kidambi Srikanth advanced to the Men’s Singles second round of Hong Kong Open Badminton Championships today. In the opening round, Srikanth defeated Japan’s Koki Watanabe 21-16, 16-21, 21-9 while Lakshya beat France’s Arnaud Merklé 14-21, 21-16, 25-23.

 

 

 

In Women’s Singles, Rakshitha Ramraj and Ashmita Chaliha also advanced to the second round.

Leaders of Quad countries met in Manila today on the sidelines of ASEAN Summit. At the meeting, Prime Minister Narendra Modi said, Manila and Quad have shared an age-old and special bond. He said cooperation among the four countries covered a wide range of areas, including maritime security, trusted supply chains, emerging technologies and disaster response. The Prime Minister said, holding a Quad meeting once again in the historic city of Manila, marks an important milestone. He called for setting concrete goals to strengthen cooperation among the four member countries in the next phase.

 

 

 

During the meeting, US President Donald Trump highlighted tha Quad’s revival and added that their cooperation has grown. He said, these countries are the four corners of a free, open, stable and most prosperous Indo-Pacific. Mr. Trump said, they have outstanding relationships and coordinate closely on matters of regional security and economic diplomacy. Japanese PM Sanae Takaichi and Australian PM Anthony Albanese were also present in the meeting.

 

 

The leaders opposed unilateral attempts to change the status quo through force or coercion and expressed concern over economic coercion, including arbitrary export restrictions.

Earlier today, Prime Minister Modi addressed the 23rd ASEAN-India Summit in Manila. He highlighted the growing partnership between India and ASEAN and called for greater cooperation to ensure peace, stability and prosperity in the Indo-Pacific region. The Prime Minister congratulated Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. on his successful chairship of ASEAN. Mr Modi said, India’s Act East policy had given India-ASEAN relations a new momentum and depth over the past several years.

                        

 

Highlighting the expansion of bilateral cooperation, PM Modi said the partnership, built on shared culture and heritage, was now expanding into new areas such as digital technologies, defence and space.

 

 

Referring to the global situation, PM Modi observed that the world had faced one crisis after another over the past few years. He said the summit’s theme, “Navigating Our Future Together,” held particular significance in the current global context. He added that India and ASEAN possessed the capabilities and shared resolve to make the region a symbol of peace and stability. India and ASEAN agreed to deepen cooperation on disaster management and early warning systems.

 

 

 

Expressing confidence in the outcome of the summit, he said the meeting would elevate the Comprehensive Strategic Partnership to new heights and contribute to building a secure, inclusive and prosperous Indo-Pacific.

 

 

 

Later, Prime Minister Modi attended the 21st East Asia Summit in Manila. PM Modi called for stronger regional cooperation and emphasised the importance of dialogue and diplomacy in addressing key regional and international challenges. He also rolled out rolls out seafarers’ safety initiative to bolster maritime security at East Asia Summit.

 

 

 

The summit brought together leaders of ASEAN member states and their eight dialogue partners to discuss regional and international issues.

 

 

 Our correspondent covering the Summit has more on the outcomes of ASEAN- India Summit and East Asia Summit.

 

 

 

“Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s visit to Manila, resulted in several important outcomes aimed at strengthening India’s engagement with ASEAN and East Asian countries.

 

 

 

During the 23rd ASEAN-India Summit, India proposed a long-term maritime cooperation plan, joint cyber forensics training, nuclear energy technical exchanges and an ASEAN-India Space Hackathon.

 

 

 

Other initiatives include cooperation in critical minerals, youth exchanges, enhanced scholarships at Nalanda University, a Creative Partnership Pavilion at WAVES 2027 and free e-visas for ASEAN tourists visiting India.

 

 

 

At the 21st East Asia Summit, India proposed a Seafarers’ Safety Initiative, an East Asia Summit Cyber Crime Conference at the National Forensic Science University, a Maritime Heritage Festival at Lothal and a University Conclave at Nalanda to promote academic cooperation.

 

 

 

The visit also saw the adoption of three important documents including the ASEAN-India Joint Statement on Cooperation in Disaster Management, the East Asia Summit Leaders’ Statement on Strengthening Cooperation Against Online Scams and Related Offences. With Ishfaq Shah’s report from Manila, tripti srivastava, AKASHVANI NEWS.

 

 

 

Prime Minister Modi has since departed for New Delhi after concluding his two day visit to Philippines.

Prime Minister Narendra Modi today held a series of bilateral meetings with leaders of the Philippines, Thailand and Singapore on the sidelines of the ASEAN-India Summit and East Asia Summit.

 

 

Prime Minister Modi and Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. discussed ways to strengthen bilateral cooperation in defence, security, trade and investment. The Ministry of External Affairs said, the two leaders reviewed their Strategic Partnership and welcomed the growing cooperation in Defence, Space, Railway infrastructure, Financial Technology and Trade.

 

 

The two leaders exchanged views on key regional and global developments and reaffirmed their commitment to expanding bilateral ties. The Ministry said, defence cooperation remains an important pillar of the partnership, with India supplying BrahMos supersonic cruise missiles to the Philippines in 2024.

India’s electronic goods exports registered strong growth of 44 per cent during April-September this year increasing from over 22 billion dollars in the corresponding period of 2025-26 to around 32 billion dollars. While smartphones continued to account for the largest share of the electronics export basket, non-smartphone electronics recorded significantly faster growth, reflecting the broadening and diversification of India’s electronics exports across components, printed circuit boards, communication equipment, memory products and storage devices.

 

 

 

Exports of smartphones increased by over 35 per cent, from 13 billion dollars in April-September last year to over 18 billion dollars during April-September this year.

 

 

Non-smartphone electronics exports recorded a growth of over 56 per cent.

The draft electoral roll under the Special Summary Revision 2027 published in Uttar Pradesh today, with claims and objections to be accepted from November 17 to December 16.

 

 

According to the list state’s electorate has increased by around 18.84 lakh since the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls.

 

 

As per the draft electoral roll for the Special Summary Revision (SSR) 2027, the state’s total number of electorate is 13 crore 58 lakh 68 thousand and 905.

 

 

Chief Electoral officer Navdeep Rinwa said that the claims and objections can be filed from today to 16th next month. The disposal of claims and objections is scheduled to be completed by December 28, with the final electoral roll set to be published on January 4, 2027.

The Cyclonic Storm “Akvan” prevailing over South and adjoining Westcentral Bay of Bengal has moved slowly northwards at a slow pace of three kilometer per hour during the past 6 hours. It is moving closer to the coastal states of Tamilnadu, Andhra and Odisha and is likely to intensify further in the coming days. The India Meteorological Department has warned of heavy to very heavy rainfall and strong winds along the coastal areas. More from our Andhra Pradesh correspondent –

 

 

“Cyclonic Storm Akvan over the Bay of Bengal is likely to intensify further and move towards the Andhra Pradesh coast. The India Meteorological Department says the storm is expected to become a Severe Cyclonic Storm tonight and a Very Severe Cyclonic Storm by Thursday morning.

 

 

 

It is expected to continue moving towards the northwest and cross the Andhra Pradesh and Yanam coasts between Nellore and Tuni around noon on Friday, as a Very Severe Cyclonic Storm. Wind speeds may reach 120 to 130 kilometres per hour, with gusts up to 145 kilometres per hour.

 

 

 

The IMD has forecast heavy rainfall at isolated places over Coastal Andhra Pradesh tomorrow. Heavy to very heavy rainfall is likely at several places on Thursday and Friday, with extremely heavy rainfall possible at isolated places.

 

 

 

Fishermen have been advised not to venture into the affected areas for the next four days. Allu Murali, Akashvani News, Vijayawada.”

 

 

 

Our Chennai Correspondent has filed this report:

 

 

 

“The cyclone is very likely to move slowly and intensify further into a Severe Cyclonic Storm tonight . The cyclone is likely to move northwestwards and intensify further into a very severe cyclonic storm around 19th November morning and continue  moving northwestward,.  Akvan will then turn into a severe cyclonic storm and  cross Andhra Pradesh & Yanam coasts between Nellore and Visakhapatnam, around noon of 20th with wind speed gusting upto 145 kmph. According to the weather department,  moderate to heavy rains are likely over  isolated places in  Northern Tamilnadu in the coming days.

The Commission for Air Quality Management Sub-Committee has revoked GRAP Stage III in Delhi in view of a downward trend, with the air quality index reaching 204 today. The CAQM however, said that all actions under GRAP Stages I and II and restrictions as per order passed 30th of last month shall remain in force. The restriction includes restriction of outdoor construction works across Delhi NCR. It has given exemption to construction works related to state duties and national interest. The circular also directs State Government and private offices to operate with up to 50 percent of the staff strength attending physically.
